what: The Cover Letter Maker writes a clear, well-structured cover letter from a short form: the job, the company, your contact details, your experience and two to four strengths or achievements.
It uses carefully written sentence templates, not AI, so nothing you type leaves your device. Empty optional fields are simply left out, so the letter never shows gaps or placeholders.
The finished letter is fully editable on the page. Download it as a PDF (A4 or Letter), a Word .docx file or plain text, copy it, or print it.
uses: A letter to send with your CV for any job.
Copy the text into the body of an email.
Paste it into the cover letter box on a job portal.
Wording for people with no work experience yet.
Highlight transferable strengths for a new field.
Try different tones and wording before you write your own.
tutorial: Type the job title and the company. Add the hiring manager's name and where you saw the job if you know them.
Your name, email, phone and city appear at the top. Leave out anything you do not want to share.
Write two to four short strengths or achievements, such as "Increased sales by 20%" or "Fluent in Spanish".
Optional: one line about what attracts you to them, such as "your focus on healthy food".
Formal for most jobs, Friendly for small or creative companies, Short for quick email applications.
Click anywhere in the letter to change words. Press Different wording for another version.
Press Make PDF, or download Word or .txt, copy the text, or print.
features: Optional fields are left out smoothly, never shown as blanks.
Formal, friendly, or short and direct.
Change any word right in the letter.
A4 or Letter PDF, a .docx file that opens in Word or Google Docs, or plain text.
Arabic, Chinese and other scripts print correctly in the PDF.
Get a fresh version of the same letter with one tap.
Works offline. Your details are saved only in this browser.

example.title: Worked example: a marketing assistant
example.text: Amina enters Marketing Assistant at Green Leaf Foods, 3 years of experience as a sales assistant, and three strengths. With the Formal tone the letter opens "I am writing to apply for the Marketing Assistant position at Green Leaf Foods, as advertised on LinkedIn", lists her strengths as bullet points, adds "What draws me to Green Leaf Foods is your focus on healthy, local food", and ends with "Yours sincerely, Amina Yusuf". She changes one sentence in the preview and downloads a one-page A4 PDF.

tips: Use numbers where you can: "served 80 customers a day" is stronger than "served many customers".
Match your strengths to words in the job advert.
Find the hiring manager's name on the advert or the company website if you can.
Keep it to one page. Short and specific beats long and general.
Read it out loud once before sending, and check the company name is spelled right.
Send it with a matching CV made with the Resume Maker.
problems: The letter did not change when I edited the form
Once you edit the letter itself, the form no longer overwrites your changes. Press Undo my edits to rebuild it from the form.
Shorten your strengths or the why-this-company line, choose the Short tone, or remove extra paragraphs in the preview.
The Word file looks slightly different
Word uses its own fonts (Georgia or Arial). The text and order are the same; adjust the font in Word if you like.
The date format is wrong for my country
Choose No date and type the date yourself in the preview.
